name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Build a self-review loop where every prompt update triggers an automated check against the last 100 tasks. The engine runs the new prompt on the same batch, compares outputs, and flags regressions or gains. Trade-off: we accept slower updates for higher confidence that changes don’t break existing workflows.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower updates—it’s that comparing outputs on the same batch of 100 tasks won’t catch edge cases the model hasn’t seen before. A better alternative is to run the new prompt against a *diverse* set of fresh tasks, not just recycled ones, to surface hidden regressions. Settle it by testing both: measure how often the batch method misses regressions vs. how often the diverse set catches them, then decide based on the delta.
